content.thinking:
I'm planning out a hunched swamp troll model, about 2.6 meters tall with oversized hands, shoulders, a small head, tusks, moss, loincloth, and a club, using only the known builder API to construct it safely.

Working through the color palette (mottled green-teal skin, lighter belly, moss, leather, iron, bone tusks) and the body geometry starting from the pelvis, legs, shins, feet, and toes with capsules and claws.

Now I'm building out the torso with a belly bulge and chest capsule, hunching the shoulders forward with the head pushed ahead for that troll stance, then starting on the arms with pauldron shoulders and tapered upper arm and forearm capsules.

For the right arm I'm figuring out how the club rests—tilted and resting against the fist rather than needing floor contact—with a spiked bulb head on top. Then I move to the head, placing a scaled skull sphere and jaw capsule.

Now I'm adding tusks jutting up from the lower jaw, glowing yellow eyes with pupils, a brow ridge, sideways ear spikes, and a warty nose, and considering how to scatter warts across the torso surface, though I'm unsure the scatter function will work on that part.

For texture I'll add moss clumps as simple spheres on the shoulders and back, plus a row of dorsal spines angled backward. For gear, I'm sketching a loincloth panel extruded at the front and figuring out how to form the belt as a closed ring shape.

Still working out the belt geometry...

Now I'm placing a bone necklace as small capsules arced across the chest, then building pauldrons from hemisphere domes with studs and spikes at the shoulders, and starting on fist-shaped hands with knuckle details.

Still building body proportions...

Now I'm planning helper functions: a sphere-maker for rounded parts, a spike-maker for tusks and teeth with directional vectors, and an extrude function for the loincloth with a sharp-pointed outline hanging below the waist.

I'm figuring out the loincloth's exact placement relative to the belly and pelvis spheres so it doesn't clip oddly, positioning the front panel near the belt buckle and adding a flipped back panel behind the pelvis.
